  "text": "On Friday evening, Mara put the carrier bag on a kitchen chair. Through the thin white plastic she could see her father’s slippers, pressed sole to sole. She had carried it that way on the bus, holding the handles together with both hands.

There was milk in his fridge and half an onion wrapped in the paper from a loaf. She shut the door before the motor stopped.

Her brother called at nine. He was still trying to change his flight.

‘There’s nothing you need to come back for tonight,’ she said.

He asked about the shop.

‘I’ve got the keys.’

‘You’ll have to put something up.’

She looked towards the chair. Her father’s trousers were in the bag too, folded by somebody who had left the belt threaded through the loops.

‘I’ll go in tomorrow.’

After the call she washed the cup she had used and left his beside the sink. There was a brown line inside it. On the windowsill stood a jar of instant coffee with a teaspoon pushed down into the granules.

She checked the front door, although she had locked it when she came in. Then she checked her own bag for the shop keys. They were attached to a small metal shoe, a souvenir from a holiday she could not remember him taking.

Before going upstairs, she set an alarm for seven. She did not know what time people began arriving with things to collect, and there was nobody she wanted to telephone to ask."
